The 2023–24 season was the 137th in the history of [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], their 32nd season in the [[Premier League]] and their 49th consecutive season in the top flight of [[Football in England|English football]]. It was the club's second season under the management of [[Erik ten Hag]].

A campaign marred by injuries saw the club finish eighth in the Premier League, their worst position since [[1989–90 Manchester United F.C. season|1989–90]], with a negative goal difference.<ref>{{cite news |first=Rob |last=Dawson |title=Man Utd wrap up worst ever Premier League spot |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/story/_/id/40172669/man-united-premier-league-worst-ever-finish |website=ESPN |date=19 May 2024 |accessdate=20 May 2024 }}</ref> United were knocked out of the [[2023–24 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] in the fourth round by the previous season's final opponents, [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]], and recorded their worst-ever [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] group stage performance, finishing bottom of their group with just four points. In the [[2023–24 FA Cup|FA Cup]] they almost suffered a humiliating exit at the hands of second tier [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]] in the semi final, throwing away a 3–0 lead before winning on penalties. This meant they reached the [[2024 FA Cup final|final]] for the second consecutive season where they faced cross-city rivals [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in a repeat of the previous year's [[2023 FA Cup final|showpiece]]. In a match they were widely considered underdogs, United won 2–1, marking the first time since [[2016–17 Manchester United F.C. season|2017]] that they won a trophy in consecutive seasons.

This was the first season since [[2010–11 Manchester United F.C. season|2010–11]] without goalkeeper [[David de Gea]] and defender [[Phil Jones (footballer, born 1992)|Phil Jones]], both of whom left the club upon the expiry of their contracts. With their departures, United were initially without a [[List of Premier League winning players|Premier League winner]] in their squad for the first time since the competition's inaugural season in [[1992–93 Manchester United F.C. season|1992–93]], and without a player who had played under [[Alex Ferguson]] for the first time since 1974.<ref>{{cite news |title=Who is Man Utd's longest-serving player? |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/who-is-now-man-utd-longest-serving-player-after-david-de-gea-departure |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=10 July 2023 |access-date=13 July 2023 }} </ref> However, the re-signing of [[Jonny Evans]], who won three Premier League titles with the club between 2006 and 2015, meant that was no longer the case.<ref>{{cite news |title=Jonny Evans signs for United |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/jonny-evans-signs-a-one-year-contract-with-man-utd-official-statement |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=1 September 2023 |access-date=17 November 2023 }}</ref>

On 24 December, Manchester United announced that the club had agreed a deal with [[Jim Ratcliffe]] to purchase a 25% stake in the club.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67815642 |title=Manchester United: Sir Jim Ratcliffe agrees deal to buy 25% stake |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=24 December 2023 |access-date=20 August 2024}}</ref> On 20 February, the investment was confirmed as complete, with Trawlers Ltd acquiring a 27.7% share in the club.<ref>{{Cite web |date=20 February 2024 |title=Manchester United plc and Trawlers Ltd Announce the Successful Completion of Sir Jim Ratcliffe's Minority Investment |url=https://www.ineos.com/news/ineos-group/manchester-united-plc-and-trawlers-ltd-announce-the-successful-completion-of-sir-jim-ratcliffes-minority-investment/ |access-date=20 August 2024 |website=ineos.com }}</ref>

== Pre-season and friendlies ==
On 27 March 2023, United announced a tour of the [[United States]], with [[Exhibition game#Club football|friendly matches]] against [[Wrexham A.F.C.|Wrexham]] – who are co-owned by actors [[Ryan Reynolds]] and [[Rob McElhenney]] and who also had former United goalkeeper [[Ben Foster (footballer)|Ben Foster]] in their squad – in [[San Diego]],<ref>{{cite news |title=United to play Wrexham AFC in San Diego |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-to-play-wrexham-afc-in-san-diego-as-part-of-summer-tour-2023--to-the-united-states |access-date=5 April 2023 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=27 March 2023}}</ref> and [[Borussia Dortmund]] in Las Vegas.<ref>{{cite news |title=United to face Dortmund in Las Vegas on Tour 2023 |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-announce-tour-2023-match-v-borussia-dortmund-in-las-vegas-usa |access-date=5 April 2023 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=4 April 2023}}</ref> On 12 May, the club announced their third and fourth pre-season friendlies in the US against [[Arsenal F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry|fierce rivals]] [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] in New York City,<ref>{{cite news |title=United to play Arsenal in New York during Tour 2023 |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-to-play-arsenal-in-new-york-during-tour-2023 |access-date=3 May 2023 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=28 April 2023}}</ref> and in [[Houston]] against [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], which will be played one day after Wrexham game.<ref>{{cite news |date=12 May 2023 |title=United set to play Real Madrid in Houston |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-to-play-real-madrid-friendly-in-houston-during-tour-2023 |access-date=15 May 2023}}</ref> A fifth friendly, the first based in the UK, against [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] in Edinburgh was also added to the pre-season calendar.<ref>{{cite news |title=United to play Lyon in Edinburgh |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-to-play-friendly-v-olympique-lyonnais-in-edinburgh-scotland |access-date=16 May 2023 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=16 May 2023}}</ref> On 25 May, the club announced a friendly against [[Leeds United F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry|Roses rivals]] and [[EFL Championship]] club [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] in [[Oslo]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Fixture news: United set to play Leeds in Oslo |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-announce-preseason-friendly-v-leeds-in-oslo-norway |access-date=25 May 2023 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=25 May 2023}}</ref> A seventh match, against [[Athletic Bilbao]] in [[Dublin]], was announced on 13 June.<ref>{{cite news |title=United to play Athletic Bilbao in Dublin |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-to-play-pre-season-friendly-v-athletic-bilbao-in-dublin |access-date=13 June 2023 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=13 June 2023}}</ref> On 29 June, the club announced a home friendly against French club [[RC Lens|Lens]], to be played the day before the match against Athletic Bilbao.<ref>{{cite news |title=United announce Old Trafford friendly |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/manchester-united-announce-old-trafford-pre-season-friendly-v-lens |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=29 June 2023 |accessdate=30 June 2023 }}</ref>

United won their first match of pre-season against Leeds 2–0, thanks to second-half goals from substitutes [[Noam Emeran]] and [[Joe Hugill]],<ref>{{cite news |first=Adam |last=Bostock |title=Manchester United 2 Leeds United 0 |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/leeds-united-v-man-utd-match-report-and-video-highlights-hub-12-july-2023 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=12 July 2023 |accessdate=26 July 2023 }}</ref> while [[Donny van de Beek]]'s goal against Lyon gave them their second win in Edinburgh.<ref>{{cite news |first=Adam |last=Higgins |title=Manchester United 1 Lyon 0 |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-v-lyon-match-report-and-video-highlights-hub-19-july-2023 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=19 July 2023 |accessdate=26 July 2023 }}</ref> In the first game of the United States tour, first-half goals from newly appointed captain [[Bruno Fernandes]] and [[Jadon Sancho]] gave United a 2–0 win over Arsenal; they also won the post-match exhibition penalty shoot-out 5–3.<ref>{{cite news |first=Joe |last=Ganley |title=Arsenal 0 Manchester United 2 |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/arsenal-v-man-utd-match-report-and-video-highlights-hub-22-july-2023 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=23 July 2023 |accessdate=26 July 2023 }}</ref> With their match against Real Madrid scheduled for Houston the next day, United fielded a team made up largely of under-21 players against Wrexham on 25 July. They went 2–0 down in the first half, though [[Marc Jurado]] pulled a goal back on the stroke of half-time; however, Dan Gore was sent off early in the second half and a third Wrexham goal completed a 3–1 defeat for United.<ref>{{cite news |first=Courtney |last=Hill |title=Report: United 1 Wrexham 3 |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/match-report-and-video-highlights-hub-from-man-utd-v-wrexham-on-26-july-2023 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=26 July 2023 |accessdate=26 July 2023 }}</ref> They then suffered a second loss in as many days when goals from [[Jude Bellingham]] and [[Joselu]] gave Real Madrid a 2–0 win in Houston; newly signed goalkeeper [[André Onana]] made his debut in the game, playing the full 90 minutes.<ref>{{cite news |first=Adam |last=Marshall |title=Match report: Real Madrid 2 United 0 |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/match-report-and-highlights-real-madrid-v-man-utd-27-july-2023 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=27 July 2023 |accessdate=27 July 2023 }}</ref> Manchester United's tour of the United States ended with a 3–2 defeat against Borussia Dortmund at the Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas on 31 July. [[Diogo Dalot]] put United ahead in the 24th minute, but [[Donyell Malen]] scored twice in two minutes just before half-time to give Dortmund the lead. [[Antony (footballer, born 2000)|Antony]] levelled the scores before [[Youssoufa Moukoko]] secured the win for the Germans.<ref>{{cite news |first=James |last=Tuck |title=Match report and highlights: United v Borussia Dortmund |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/match-report-and-highlights-man-utd-v-borussia-dortmund-31-july-2023 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=31 July 2023 |accessdate=14 August 2023 }}</ref>

The Reds returned to winning ways with a 3–1 comeback win over Lens at Old Trafford. [[Florian Sotoca]] put the visitors ahead after chipping Onana from the edge of the centre circle in the first half, before [[Marcus Rashford]], Antony and [[Casemiro]] scored in the second period to turn the game around for United.<ref>{{cite news |first=Oliver |last=Yew |title=Man Utd 3-1 RC Lens: Andre Onana beaten by halfway line stunner but hosts roar back for victory |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/manchester-united-vs-rc-lens/stats/488329 |website=SkySports.com |publisher=Sky Sports |date=5 August 2023 |accessdate=6 August 2023 }}</ref> The following day, a second string United side drew 1–1 with Athletic Bilbao in Dublin. The La Liga team scored first through [[Nico Williams]], but an added time equaliser from [[Facundo Pellistri]] meant that United ended their pre-season campaign with a draw.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/manchester-united-vs-athletic-bilbao/live/482494 |website=SkySports.com |title=Manchester United 1-1 Athletic Bilbao – Pre-season: Report, recap and reaction |date=6 August 2023 |access-date=8 Aug 2023 }}</ref>

== Premier League ==
The [[2023–24 Premier League]] fixtures were released on 15 June 2023.<ref>{{cite news |title=Revealed: United's 2023/24 Premier League fixtures |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-premier-league-fixtures-2023-24-revealed-thursday-15-june-2023 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=15 June 2023 |access-date=15 June 2023 }}</ref>

The league season began with a home win against [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] on 14 August. After a scoreless first half, [[Raphaël Varane]] scored the game's only goal with a 76th-minute header. Named in the starting line-up, [[Mason Mount]] and [[André Onana]] made their debuts for United.<ref>{{cite web |title=Report: United 1 Wolves 0 |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/match-report-and-video-highlights-manchester-united-v-wolverhampton-wanderers-14-august-2023 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=14 August 2023 |accessdate=15 August 2023 }}</ref> Five days later, United suffered an away defeat to [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]]. [[Pape Matar Sarr]] opened the scoring for the home side in the 49th minute, and an [[own goal]] from [[Lisandro Martínez]] doubled their lead seven minutes from the end.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tottenham Hotspur 2-0 Manchester United: Spurs earn boss Ange Postecoglou first Premier League win |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66482710 |website=BBC Sport |date=19 August 2023 |accessdate=2 September 2023 }}</ref> United then hosted [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] the following weekend, coming into the match on a 30-game unbeaten run at home; however, that streak was put in jeopardy as United conceded two goals in the opening five minutes. [[Christian Eriksen]] pulled one back in the first half, before [[Casemiro]] and [[Bruno Fernandes]] secured the comeback win with a goal each either side of a second-half red card for Forest's [[Joe Worrall (footballer)|Joe Worrall]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Manchester United 3-2 Nottingham Forest: Bruno Fernandes' penalty completes turnaround as hosts win from 2-0 down |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66552608 |website=BBC Sport |date=26 August 2023 |accessdate=2 September 2023 }}</ref>

The month of September started with a loss away to Arsenal. [[Marcus Rashford]] struck first, but [[Martin Ødegaard]] levelled the score 35 seconds after restart of the game. In the second half, a [[Video Assistant Referee|VAR]] check saw an Arsenal penalty claim overturned and another check led to an effort by [[Alejandro Garnacho]] being ruled out as offside. The Gunners then struck twice in injury time to win the match.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Arsenal 3-1 Manchester United: Declan Rice and Gabriel Jesus injury-time goals stun Red Devils |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66631567 |website=BBC Sport |date=3 September 2023|accessdate=6 September 2023 }}</ref> Following an [[FIFA International Match Calendar|international break]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=When are the international breaks this season? |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/international-breaks-2324#:~:text=Nations%20League-,September%202%202024,-September%2010%2C%202024}}</ref> United hosted [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]]; their 31-game unbeaten run at home ended with former United player [[Danny Welbeck]] scoring the opening goal. In the second half, Brighton scored two more goals, though substitute [[Hannibal Mejbri]] scored a consolation goal in the 73rd-minute from outside the box, marking his first goal of the season. The Red Devils would then win against [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] away the following weekend, Bruno Fernandes scoring the only goal with a 45th-minute volley that would later win [[Premier League Goal of the Month]]. The month of September closed with a 1–0 defeat to [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] at home, marking back-to-back defeats at home for the Reds.

Manchester United would host [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] at home to kick off October, where [[Mathias Jensen]]'s first-half effort for the Bees saw them lead 1–0, threatening to make it United's third consecutive loss at home for the first time since the [[1978–79 Manchester United F.C. season|1978-79 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Manchester United 2-1 Brentford: Scott McTominay's late double salvages dramatic victory |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66969161#:~:text=United%20were%20staring%20at%20a%20third%20successive%20home%20league%20loss%20for%20the%20first%20time%20since%201979%20thanks%20to%20Mathias%20Jensen%27s%20first%2Dhalf%20effort}}</ref> However, with three minutes of stoppage-time left, [[Scott McTominay]] was brought on and scored two goals within three minutes, salvaging a win for the Reds. Two weeks later United travelled to [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]], wearing black armbands in remembrance of [[Bobby Charlton]], following the earlier news of his passing. Scott McTominay opened the scoring in the first half, but the home-team quickly responded via a penalty from [[Oli McBurnie]]. With the scoreline level until the 77th-minute, [[Diogo Dalot]] fired home his first goal of the season beyond the penalty area to win the match. The month closed with United hosting [[Manchester derby|rivals]] [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]]; [[Erling Haaland]] put City ahead with a penalty in the first half after [[Rasmus Højlund]] was penalised for dragging down [[Rodri (footballer, born 1996)|Rodri]] inside the box. After Onana saved a far-post header from Haaland, a near-identical play saw Haaland double City's lead before half-time courtesy of a cross from [[Bernardo Silva]]. In the 86th minute, [[Phil Foden]] scored the third goal, cementing a 3–0 defeat for United.

== FA Cup ==
As a Premier League side, United entered the [[2023–24 FA Cup]] in the third round and were drawn away to [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]],<ref>{{cite news |first=Joe |last=Nelson |title=Man Utd learn FA Cup Third Round opponents |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-learn-fa-cup-third-round-opponents-3-december-2023 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=3 December 2023 |access-date=7 December 2023 }}</ref> with the match to be played on 8 January 2024.<ref>{{cite news |first=Sam |last=Carney |title=Man Utd Emirates FA Cup third-round date at Wigan announced |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-emirates-fa-cup-third-round-date-at-wigan-announced |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=7 December 2023 |access-date=7 December 2023 }}</ref> United won 2–0 thanks to a long-range strike from Diogo Dalot in the first half, followed by a Bruno Fernandes penalty. They were then drawn against either [[Newport County A.F.C.|Newport County]] or [[Eastleigh F.C.|Eastleigh]] in the fourth round.<ref>{{cite news |title=FA Cup Fourth Round: United drawn away again |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/draw-made-for-2023-24-fa-cup-fourth-round |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=8 January 2024 |access-date=8 January 2024 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |first=Adam |last=Bostock |title=FA Cup: date confirmed for United's fourth-round tie |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/date-set-for-man-utd-fourth-round-tie-in-2023-24-emirates-fa-cup |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=11 January 2024 |access-date=11 January 2024 }}</ref> Newport were confirmed as their opponents when they beat Eastleigh 3–1 in a replay on 16 January 2024.<ref>{{cite news |title=FA Cup: Eastleigh 1-3 Newport County – Exiles set up fourth-round tie against Manchester United |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67984505 |website=BBC Sport |date=16 January 2024 |accessdate=18 January 2024 }}</ref> On 28 January, United won at [[Rodney Parade]] 4–2 courtesy of goals from Fernandes, Kobbie Mainoo, Antony and Rasmus Højlund.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/match-report-newport-county-v-man-utd-fa-cup-28-january-2024 |title=Match report: Newport County 2 Manchester United 4 |website=ManUtd.com |date=28 January 2024 |access-date=5 February 2024 }}</ref> On the same day, [[Bristol City F.C.|Bristol City]] or [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] were drawn as their next opponents, with the match taking place on 28 February.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/fa-cup-fifth-round-draw-details-28-january-2024 |title=FA Cup fifth-round draw details |website=ManUtd.com |date=28 January 2024 |access-date=5 February 2024 }}</ref> On 7 February, Nottingham Forest were confirmed as United's next opponents thanks to their 5–3 win on penalties.<ref>{{cite news |title=Nottingham Forest 1-1 Bristol City (5-3 on pens): Premier League hosts edge to win on penalties |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68235324 |website=BBC Sport |date=7 February 2024 |accessdate=12 February 2024 }}</ref> United won at [[City Ground]] 1–0 thanks to a late effort from Casemiro.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/match-report-man-utd-fa-cup-fifth-round-trip-to-nottingham-forest |title=Match report from Nott&#x27;m Forest 0 Man Utd 1 in FA Cup fifth round {{!}} 28 February 2024 {{!}} Manchester United |publisher=ManUtd.com |date=28 February 2024 |access-date=15 March 2024 }}</ref>

With [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]]'s 3–0 win over [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] in the fifth round, United were drawn against their [[Liverpool F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry|rivals]] in the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-learn-potential-emirates-fa-cup-quarter-final-opponents-2023-24 |title=Man Utd learn potential Emirates FA Cup quarter final opponents 2023/24 |website=ManUtd.com |date=28 February 2024 |access-date=28 February 2024 }}</ref> The tie was played on 17 March. United took an early lead thanks to Scott McTominay, but going into half time, goals from [[Alexis Mac Allister]] and [[Mohamed Salah]] saw Liverpool take a 2–1 lead. Antony scored a late equaliser to take the match into extra time, although Rashford missed the chance to score an injury-time winner. Near the end of the first half of extra time, [[Harvey Elliott]] gave Liverpool the lead, but in the second half, Rashford equalised to make the score 3–3. In injury time, [[Amad Diallo]] scored the winning goal, and was sent off for taking his shirt off in the celebrations as he was given a yellow card prior to scoring.<ref>{{cite news |url= https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/match-report-from-man-utd-v-liverpool-fa-cup-17-march-2024 |title=Match report for Man Utd 4 Liverpool 3 |publisher=ManUtd.com |date=17 March 2024 |access-date=20 March 2024 }}</ref>

United were drawn against Coventry City in the semi-finals. They faced each other at [[Wembley Stadium]] on 21 April, with United winning 4–2 on penalties after giving up a 3–0 lead in the second thanks to Coventry striker [[Haji Wright]]'s equalizer in [[stoppage time]] of the second half.

United faced [[Manchester City]] for a second consecutive [[Manchester Derby]] FA Cup Final. [[Alejandro Garnacho]] opened the scoring following a miscommunication between [[Joško Gvardiol]] and [[Stefan Ortega]]. Following a disallowed [[Marcus Rashford]] goal, [[Kobbie Mainoo]] quickly scored United's second. [[Jerémy Doku]] got one back for City late on but it wasn't enough as United picked up their 13th FA Cup trophy.

== EFL Cup ==
As United were competing in [[UEFA competitions|UEFA competition]] in 2023–24 as the [[2023 EFL Cup final|reigning champions]] of the competition, they entered the [[2023–24 EFL Cup]] in the third round in September. They were drawn at home to [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-learn-opponents-for-2023-24-carabao-cup-third-round |title=Confirmed: United's Carabao Cup third-round opponents |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=30 August 2023 |access-date=31 August 2023 }}</ref> They beat Palace 3–0 thanks to goals from [[Alejandro Garnacho]], [[Casemiro]] and [[Anthony Martial]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Manchester United 3-0 Crystal Palace: Hosts begin Carabao Cup defence with comfortable victory |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66850672 |website=BBC Sport |date=26 September 2023 |accessdate=18 January 2024 }}</ref> In the fourth round, they were given another home draw against [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]], in a repeat of the [[2023 EFL Cup final]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Mark |last=Froggatt |title=Fixtures news: Carabao Cup fourth-round draw |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-learn-opposition-from-2023-carabao-cup-fourth-round-draw |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=27 September 2023 |access-date=28 September 2023 }}</ref> This time they lost 3–0, with goals from [[Miguel Almirón]] and [[Lewis Hall (footballer)|Lewis Hall]] in the first half and a third from [[Joe Willock]] in the second.

== UEFA Champions League ==
=== Group stage ===
{{Main|2023–24 UEFA Champions League group stage}}
Having finished third in the [[2022–23 Premier League]], United qualified for the [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League]]. They entered the competition in the group stage, which was drawn on 31 August 2023, with United in pot 2 along with [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], [[Inter Milan]], [[Borussia Dortmund]], [[Atlético Madrid]], [[RB Leipzig]], [[FC Porto|Porto]] and Arsenal. After losing their first two matches in Group A to [[Bayern Munich]] and [[Galatasaray]], United responded with a 1-0 win over [[FC Copenhagen]], [[Harry Maguire]] scoring the winning goal and [[Andre Onana]] saving a last minute [[penalty kick]]. However United gave away two-goal leads against Copenhagen and Galatasaray, causing eventual elimination from the competition after a 1–0 defeat to Bayern.<ref>{{cite news |title=Confirmed: Champions League group-stage pots |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-learn-champions-league-group-stage-draw-pots-for-2023-24-season |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=30 August 2023 |accessdate=31 August 2023 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Confirmed: United's Champions League opponents |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-group-stage-opponents-confirmed-for-2023-24-uefa-champions-league |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=31 August 2023 |accessdate=31 August 2023 }}</ref>
